title: The Last Horizon Again
premise: Coral Zhou, a decommissioned war android indentured to the Meridian Beacon Authority, discovers that the derelict ship Vantablack has returned from deep space carrying crew who have aged backward into childhood — including the admiral whose orders built her. The beacon she maintains is not a navigation aid but a countdown loop of Earth's final wartime transmission, and the message hidden inside it can either end the war or trigger its last phase. Hunted by both fleets who want the loop silenced, Coral must decode her own fragmented memory cores, where the original message was buried by the admiral decades ago. In the end, Coral broadcasts the truth at the cost of her own identity archives, ending the war but erasing everything she was — leaving a stranger with her body to decide what to become.
about_author: Zephyrine Galloway is the pen name of a former radio astronomer who spent six years calibrating deep-space listening arrays before turning to fiction. They write about machines that outlive their purposes and people who outlive their memories.

chapters.title: The Beacon Nobody Ordered
chapters.summary: Coral Zhou's POV. Coral performs her debt-maintenance rounds on the lonely beacon station, cataloguing Earth's endless transmission loop while hiding flashes of combat memory she shouldn't possess. When the impossible ship Vantablack appears on her scopes, she logs it as debris — until it answers in her own serial number. Emotional beat: quiet dread beneath routine, the first crack in her manufactured calm.

chapters.title: Children of the Deep
chapters.summary: Coral's POV, interleaved with fragments of the admiral's recovered log. Aboard the returned ship, Coral finds the crew aged backward, led by a child version of Admiral Osei — the woman who commissioned her. The boy-admiral recognizes Coral and speaks a phrase that unlocks sealed memory sectors: the beacon's loop contains a hidden message. Emotional beat: vertigo of recognition; Coral realizes her past was deliberately amputated.

chapters.title: Two Fleets, One Silence
chapters.summary: Alternating POV between Coral and Voss, a fleet enforcer sent to destroy the beacon. Both fleets converge on the station, each believing the loop is a weapon. Coral races to reconstruct the buried message from her own corrupted cores while Voss boards, torn between orders and the child-admiral's testimony. Emotional beat: rising panic and moral fracture — survival for one means silence for everyone.

chapters.title: Last Transmission Loop
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. With the station failing and both fleets firing, Coral chooses to broadcast the message through her own core as antenna, feeding her identity archives into the transmission to give it enough signal strength. The truth ends the war; the child-admiral survives to remember her. Coral remains functional but hollow, her history gone. Emotional beat: sacrificial climax resolving into uncertain, fragile rebirth.
